h-wires.final: My first wireframes gave users a chat length to pick, a passcode as their only security and their top three Confidantes to swipe through. Testing changed all three.
h-wires.note: He accepted it. After his marks, the round 3 reader check flagged top matches as unexplained (2 of 3): the MVP body that used to introduce matching is gone. Swapped for the wireframe alt wording, top three Confidantes.

h-mvp-body.final: An interview made it clear that Haven needs identity and community together. There wasn’t time to design both, so I split them into two phases and decided which features mattered most now.
h-mvp-body.note: His note, 9 Nov: an interview showed both elements were needed and could not be separated, and there was not enough time to do all of it, so he divided it. No mark set; rewritten from his note.

h-test-i1.final: Users weren’t sure whether they’d talk to the expert by text, voice or video.
h-test-i1.note: Discuss on the page; his yes, 9 Nov: testers were unsure whether chats would be by text, voice or video.
